bull_bear.body:
- Home-grown Indian OEM with a trusted brand name and now a strong player in the system-integration market
- High quality product engineering skills
- Wide range of product offerings with high local content across design, hardware and software
- Major Tier-1 customer confidence
- Trusted Source status on the DoT Trusted Portal, which has improved acceptance in the switching and routing domain
- Self-sufficiency in routing and switching products, enabling more cost-efficient solutions and competitive bidding for system-integration tenders
- Recurring cash flow from managing, operating and maintaining 5 projects, operating nearly 1500 links with four Network Operations Centres
- Track record in network security - UTM deployed across Pondicherry SWAN with NIL security breach to date, plus deployments in Railways and the coal sector
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on government customers — Listed as a threat in the Company's own SWOT analysis. The Products and Solutions businesses sell largely into Telecom PSUs, Government, Public Sector, Railways, Defence and state networks (Pondicherry SWAN, BSNL-WCL, BSNL-BCCL, RailTel-WCL, APEPDCL), so revenue is tied to public tendering, budget cycles and policy continuity.
- Liquidity shortage with most customers — Listed as a threat in the SWOT analysis; customer liquidity constraints stretch collections and working capital in a tender-driven, project-based business.
- Limited high-skill manpower bench — Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis. Product engineering, firmware and network integration depend on scarce specialist talent, which is why management says the coming year's focus will be greater hiring.
- High cost of capital — Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis; expensive funding weighs on a business that must fund R&D, inventory and project execution as well as real estate development.
- R&D needs to be strengthened — Management itself flags R&D as a weakness even while new products (1G indigenous switch, NOS, UTM, SD-WAN) are the stated growth engine, so under-investment directly threatens the product roadmap.
- Increased market competition in networking products — The Company notes it maintained product sales 'despite increased market competition and various challenges', indicating competitive pressure on the switching and routing business.
- Contract renewal and renegotiation risk in the Solutions business — Solutions revenue declined because projects were in the renewal and contract renegotiation stage during the year, showing that recurring O&M revenue is exposed to re-tendering and repricing at contract expiry.
- Dependence on certifications and trusted-source status for market access — Market acceptance rests on TEC certification, clearing RDSO inspection and remaining a Trusted Source on the DoT Trusted Portal, plus compliance with the National Security Directive on the Telecommunication Sector; loss or non-renewal of any of these would restrict access to the Company's core public-sector markets.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company operates three reported business verticals - Products, Solutions and Real Estate - supported by a Service Business Unit that acts as the operations arm for maintenance, operations and repair of all OEM products it sells. The Products unit sells indigenous routers, switches, Unified Threat Manager appliances and data-centre networking platforms to Telecom, Broadband, Enterprise, Government, Public Sector, Railways and Defence customers, while the Solutions unit manages, operates and maintains turnkey network projects across the country through Network Operations Centres. The Real Estate vertical develops premium residential projects, with UmiyaBricklane at Candolim, North Goa, and Umiya Prism on Cunningham Road, Bengaluru, launched by the associated firm Umiya Buildtek.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Products:** Routers, Switches, High-capacity switches, Data centre networking products, Proprietary Network Operating System (NOS), High-performance switching platforms on disaggregated architecture with SONiC Network Operating System, TDMoIP device (Network Interface Unit) for defence, Unified Threat Manager (UTM), 1G indigenous switch (under development), Software Defined WAN (SD-WAN), Cloud Managed Services, Integrated Private 5G solution (Radio Unit, Centralised/Distributed Unit, Core Network, Network Management platform), MPLS-enabled carrier-grade switches (on roadmap)
- **Solutions:** Turnkey network projects / system integration, Network Operations Centre (NOC) based network management services, Operations and maintenance of network projects
- **Services:** Maintenance, operations and repair of all OEM products sold by the Company
- **Real Estate:** UmiyaBricklane, Candolim, North Goa, Umiya Prism, Cunningham Road, Bengaluru (launched by associated firm Umiya Buildtek)

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Consolidate the business into four dedicated pillars - Products for Telecom and Railways, Turnkey Projects/System Integration, Services, and Real Estate - which will remain the focus for the next few years
- Strengthen the indigenous product portfolio and system-integration capability, with sustained investment in R&D and in the Company's proprietary Network Operating System (NOS)
- Raise local content across design, hardware and software, leveraging Make in India policy, the National Security Directive on the Telecommunication Sector (NSDTS) and Trusted Source status on the DoT Trusted Portal
- Build out data-centre and AI networking with high-performance switching platforms based on disaggregated architecture and the SONiC Network Operating System
- Address the Private 5G opportunity with a ready integrated solution comprising Radio Unit, Centralised/Distributed Unit, Core Network and Network Management platform
- Expand the product roadmap to MPLS-enabled carrier-grade switches for Internet Service Providers, telecom operators and critical network applications
- Continue expanding the Ethernet switching portfolio with additional variants offering enhanced features, higher performance and cost-effective configurations
- Develop an indigenous 1G switch with more than 65% local content, manufactured in-house from a CKD kit
- Continue to focus on turnkey projects in network-specific areas, using new product induction (SD-WAN, UTM, Cloud Services) to drive business development in the System Integration vertical
- Advance the premium real estate strategy - UmiyaBricklane at Candolim, North Goa, and Umiya Prism on Cunningham Road, Bengaluru (launched by associated firm Umiya Buildtek)
- Grow the Defence vertical through the TDMoIP device developed for a large defence system integrator, including military-grade hardening
- Leverage proven capability in network security (UTM) to capture a larger share of that market
- Increase hiring and expand technical and research teams to support growth in networking products, technology development and real estate operations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion during FY 2025-26 was led by the Real Estate vertical and by indigenous manufacturing and R&D build-out rather than by a conventional plant capex programme; the Company states it undertook strategic initiatives towards expanding its presence in next-generation technologies, strengthening its real estate portfolio, enhancing indigenous manufacturing capabilities and increasing focus on research and development. In real estate, UmiyaBricklane at Candolim, North Goa - the Company's strategic expansion into a high-potential tourism and lifestyle destination - secured all key regulatory approvals including RERA registration and plan approvals and drew an encouraging market response with initial bookings and customer advances; the associated firm Umiya Buildtek launched Umiya Prism on Cunningham Road, Bengaluru, an ultra-luxury boutique residential project in the Central Business District, which has received RERA approval and where initial project development activities are currently underway. On the manufacturing side, the Company has commenced R&D on an indigenous 1G switch: firmware development is in progress and the switch hardware will be run from a Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit and manufactured at the Company's own factory, with roll-out expected at more than 65% local content. The Solutions footprint covers 5 projects managed, operated and maintained across the country, operating nearly 1500 links with four Network Operations Centres, extended during the year by an additional order of 50 sites under the Pondicherry SWAN project and an order from RailTel for supply of TDM/IP devices for a key Railways project. The Company also disposed of its property at Electronic City during the year, and states that the coming year's focus will be on greater hiring and R&D effort.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's data centre IT load capacity is expected to reach approximately 4.7 GW over the next three years, driven by adoption of Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, High Performance Computing and Edge Computing
- The addressable market for AI and data centre networking solutions is estimated at around Rs. 6,500 crore
- Demand for Private 5G networks is growing significantly across manufacturing, airports, railways and other industrial sectors, driven by the need for secure, reliable and dedicated communication infrastructure
- Increasing demand for reliable carrier-grade networking infrastructure among ISPs, telecom operators and critical network applications
- Induction of new products in high-capacity switches and data centre networking has gained momentum and is expected to drive future growth
- Momentum in government and public sector projects, particularly digital infrastructure, supported by favourable government policies and Make in India initiatives
- Railways remains an important market, with increased orders for switches and routers for signalling and surveillance applications and products cleared through RDSO inspection
- Trusted Source status on the DoT Trusted Portal and NSDTS regulation are improving market acceptance of the Company's switching and routing products
- Self-sufficiency in routing and switching products allows more cost-efficient solutions and more competitive bidding for system-integration tenders
- Real estate demand: UmiyaBricklane at Candolim received an encouraging market response with initial bookings and customer advances, marking expansion into a high-potential tourism and lifestyle destination
- Solutions revenue was temporarily affected by projects being in the renewal and contract renegotiation stage during the year
- The Company continues to hold a healthy order pipeline in government and public sector digital infrastructure projects, providing visibility for future growth
- Additional order of 50 sites received for the Pondicherry SWAN project
- Significant order received from RailTel for supply of TDM/IP device for a key Railways project
- Increased orders received during the year for switches and routers for deployment in Railways signalling and surveillance applications
- Managing, operating and maintaining 5 projects across the country, operating nearly 1500 links with four Network Operations Centres, which ensures robust regular cash flow
- Ongoing operations and maintenance engagements with BSNL-WCL, BSNL-BCCL, RailTel-WCL and APEPDCL, with stipulated SLAs being achieved

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Home-grown Indian OEM with a trusted brand name and now a strong player in the system-integration market
- High quality product engineering skills
- Wide range of product offerings with high local content across design, hardware and software
- Major Tier-1 customer confidence
- Trusted Source status on the DoT Trusted Portal, which has improved acceptance in the switching and routing domain
- Self-sufficiency in routing and switching products, enabling more cost-efficient solutions and competitive bidding for system-integration tenders
- Recurring cash flow from managing, operating and maintaining 5 projects, operating nearly 1500 links with four Network Operations Centres
- Track record in network security - UTM deployed across Pondicherry SWAN with NIL security breach to date, plus deployments in Railways and the coal sector

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on government customers — Listed as a threat in the Company's own SWOT analysis. The Products and Solutions businesses sell largely into Telecom PSUs, Government, Public Sector, Railways, Defence and state networks (Pondicherry SWAN, BSNL-WCL, BSNL-BCCL, RailTel-WCL, APEPDCL), so revenue is tied to public tendering, budget cycles and policy continuity.
- Liquidity shortage with most customers — Listed as a threat in the SWOT analysis; customer liquidity constraints stretch collections and working capital in a tender-driven, project-based business.
- Limited high-skill manpower bench — Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis. Product engineering, firmware and network integration depend on scarce specialist talent, which is why management says the coming year's focus will be greater hiring.
- High cost of capital — Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis; expensive funding weighs on a business that must fund R&D, inventory and project execution as well as real estate development.
- R&D needs to be strengthened — Management itself flags R&D as a weakness even while new products (1G indigenous switch, NOS, UTM, SD-WAN) are the stated growth engine, so under-investment directly threatens the product roadmap.
- Increased market competition in networking products — The Company notes it maintained product sales 'despite increased market competition and various challenges', indicating competitive pressure on the switching and routing business.
- Contract renewal and renegotiation risk in the Solutions business — Solutions revenue declined because projects were in the renewal and contract renegotiation stage during the year, showing that recurring O&M revenue is exposed to re-tendering and repricing at contract expiry.
- Dependence on certifications and trusted-source status for market access — Market acceptance rests on TEC certification, clearing RDSO inspection and remaining a Trusted Source on the DoT Trusted Portal, plus compliance with the National Security Directive on the Telecommunication Sector; loss or non-renewal of any of these would restrict access to the Company's core public-sector markets.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Consolidate the business into four dedicated pillars - Products for Telecom and Railways, Turnkey Projects/System Integration, Services, and Real Estate - which will remain the focus for the next few years
- Strengthen the indigenous product portfolio and system-integration capability, with sustained investment in R&D and in the Company's proprietary Network Operating System (NOS)
- Raise local content across design, hardware and software, leveraging Make in India policy, the National Security Directive on the Telecommunication Sector (NSDTS) and Trusted Source status on the DoT Trusted …

hero.oneLiner: Umiya Buildcon Limited (formerly MRO-TEK Realty Limited) is a home-grown Indian networking OEM that designs and makes routers, switches and security appliances with high local content, runs turnkey network integration and managed-services projects, and develops premium residential real estate.
